source.raw:
②
let P(n): \underline{1 + 3 + 5 + \text{- - -}\cdots 2n-1} = \underline{n^2}
LHS (n) = 1 + 3 + \text{- - -} 2n-1
RHS (n) = n^2
P(n): LHS(n) = RHS(n)
I want to show P(n) is true, \forall n \ge 1.
Step 1 : \underline{Basic step. n=1}
LHS (1) = 1
RHS (1) = 1^2 = 1 \quad \ge LHS(1)=RHS(1)
P(1) is true.
Step 2: \underline{Inductive step:}
I want to show P(n) \to P(n+1) , n \ge 1.
\underline{Direct proof:}
P(n) is true, i.e.,
LHS(n) = RHS(n)
LHS (n+1) = \underline{1 + 3 + 5 + \text{- - -} 2n-1} + 2n+1
= LHS(n) + 2n+1 = RHS(n)+2n+1 = n^2+2n+1
RHS(n+1) = (n+1)^2 = n^2+2n+1
